es.q: A patient is admitted to the Intensive Care Unit with severe sepsis and rapidly develops acute respiratory distress. A chest X-ray shows bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. This condition is suspected to be Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS). Describe the hallmark microscopic finding in the acu
es.m: The hallmark microscopic finding in the acute phase of Diffuse Alveolar Damage (DAD), which is the histological manifestation of ARDS, is the presence of **hyaline membranes**. es.q: A 55-year-old male is admitted to the intensive care unit following severe sepsis. He develops acute onset dyspnea, severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy, and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on chest X-ray, without evidence of left-sided heart failure. 1. Based on the clinical presentation,
es.m: 1. **Diagnosis**: The most likely diagnosis is Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), which represents the severe end of Acute Lung Injury (ALI).
